surah_rahman.name: Ar-Rahman
surah_rahman.ayah_duration_distribution: Extremely uniform. The refrain 'Fabi-ayyi ala-i Rabbikuma tukaththiban' is repeated 31 times, creating identical repeating temporal blocks of ~5.2 seconds.
surah_rahman.silence_gaps: Short, regular, and predictable breathing pauses (~1.5s to 2.5s) between verses.
surah_rahman.vad_boundaries: Highly distinct and clean speech-onsets and speech-offsets.
surah_rahman.long_vowels_madd: Short and consistent; no extreme or highly elongated vocalic chanting.
surah_rahman.acoustic_energy: Very high, clean, and continuous voice energy during the brief verse blocks.
surah_rahman.boundary_confidence: Extremely high because candidates match the nominal duration-prior perfectly.
surah_rahman.duration_ratio_behavior: Highly accurate. Since almost all verses have identical lengths, the nominal syllable ratio is close to 1.0, making the duration-prior heuristic highly effective.
surah_rahman.local_boundary_errors: Negligible. Boundaries align perfectly with the standard VAD intervals.

surah_mulk.name: Al-Mulk
surah_mulk.ayah_duration_distribution: Highly variable and non-uniform. Verse lengths range from extremely short (e.g., 4s) to very long, complex theological structures (e.g., 20s+).
surah_mulk.silence_gaps: Highly irregular and prolonged pauses, including a major 9-second silent/breath gap between Ayah 23 and 24.
surah_mulk.vad_boundaries: Difficult to detect cleanly. Deep breaths, soft whispers, and weak voice onsets/offsets create fuzzy or fragmented transitions.
surah_mulk.long_vowels_madd: Frequent and prolonged Madd elongations (~1.5s to 2.0s) at the ends of verses (e.g. end of Ayah 23).
surah_mulk.acoustic_energy: Variable energy with gradual vocal fadeouts and soft onsets that bleed into silent gaps.
surah_mulk.boundary_confidence: Low at complex transitions where the phonetic model's syllable count does not predict the prolonged breathing pause.
surah_mulk.duration_ratio_behavior: Highly erratic. Extreme variations in verse structures cause the duration-ratio heuristic to stretch boundaries late, absorbing silent intervals into adjacent verses.
surah_mulk.local_boundary_errors: Significant. Massive local temporal boundary errors occur at transitions containing prolonged Madd and long pauses, causing text to lag behind the recitation.

analytical_summary: The current engine succeeds on Surah Rahman because Rahman's highly rhythmic, uniform, and repetitive structure perfectly satisfies the duration-ratio and syllable-prior heuristics. Conversely, Surah Mulk's highly variable verse durations, complex Madd elongations, and deep, irregular breathing pauses (like the 9-second gap) completely violate the assumptions of the duration-prior heuristic, leading to severe local boundary errors where text lags behind the recitation.
